clue.text: Film star with no love for costume

indicators.note: with no tells us to drop a letter from the star's surname

parts.note: Greta Garbo, the Swedish-born Hollywood star
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A screen idol who has fallen out of love with wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O (love, a tennis zero) from GARBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, especially a distinctive outfit, much like a costume.

clue.text: Distant flicker

definitions.meaning: informal name for the handset used to switch TV channels

explanation.surface: A faint, far-off glimmer of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flicker' looks like a glimmer, but it is one who flicks between channels: the TV handset.
explanation.definitionFit: A far-off place is a synonym pair with distant; the handset you flick channels with is the TV controller.

clue.text: Forestall old boy, one getting invite after separation

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: the remainder gets the single letter, taking it inside
split the word invite into two parts, its first two letters standing apart from the rest

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: An old school chum heads off a party invitation once a couple splits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invite after separation' reads as IN VITE: 'one getting in VITE' puts A inside VITE to make VIATE, after OB.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate something is to anticipate and prevent it, which is what forestalling means.

clue.text: Ruin destroyed a not-unknown Conservative peer

indicators.note: destroyed tells us the letters of ruin are wrecked and rearranged
not means the following unknown is to be left out of the party word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: A well-known Tory lord brought to ruin and disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges RUIN to URIN; 'not' removes Y (an unknown) from TORY, leaving TOR. 'peer' is not a lord here but one who pees.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as someone who pees, a peer is one who passes water, a comic coinage.

clue.text: Agility of limbs seen flying to catch Australian tail-ender

indicators.note: to catch means the jumble holds the next letter inside it
flying limbs suggests the letters flailing into a new order
the tail-ender is the last letter, a cricket joke on the lower-order batsman

explanation.surface: A fielder's speed as limbs dive to catch an Aussie number eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges LIMBS SEEN; 'to catch' puts N, the last letter of Australian ('tail-ender'), inside it. A tail-ender in cricket is a weak batsman at the end of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quick and light on your feet is the quality of agility, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Trouble held up plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you
had means held, as in had in your hands

explanation.surface: Something went wrong and a planting was delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' turns the whole charade backwards, so 'Trouble' and 'held' end up in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a showy garden flower with tuberous roots, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Happy with hook-up? Post on social media

parts.note: up means cheerful, in good spirits
a date is a romantic meeting, an informal hook-up

explanation.surface: Pleased about a romantic encounter, someone wonders whether to tell their followers online.
explanation.definitionFit: A new status or news item put out on a feed is an update, a common verb and noun in social media use.

clue.text: Still old officer getting trapped wind

indicators.note: the officer gets trapped inside the other pieces

parts.note: a pic is a still, a photograph
Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: A retired officer is still suffering from trapped wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' is not digestive but a wind instrument; 'trapped' sounds medical but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The piccolo is a small flute, one of the woodwind family of instruments.

clue.text: Place to observe Ken's partner taking ecstasy on toilet

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, removing the drug from the doll

parts.note: Barbie, the doll whose boyfriend is Ken
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
can is slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A seedy scene: Barbie on drugs on the loo, watched from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' looks like taking drugs but means removing E from BARBIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbican is a fortified gate tower or outwork from which defenders kept watch.

clue.text: Don't picket, you say? I won't!

definitions.text: Don't picket, you say? I won't!

parts.words: Don't picket, you say? I won't!
parts.note: a strike-breaker refuses to picket; and 'picket' heard as pick it suggests the crust on a wound you should leave alone

explanation.surface: A worker replies defiantly when told not to join the picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: a strike-breaker who will not picket, and a wound crust you are told not to pick.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker crossing a picket line is called this insult; the same word names the crust over a healing wound.

clue.text: Rundown Hilton Hotel lacking robes gets three stars

indicators.note: rundown suggests a dilapidated place, so the letters are knocked into a new shape
lacking means the hotel letter is taken out of Hilton

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A shabby Hilton without bathrobes still claims a three-star rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes H (Hotel) from HILTON, leaving ILTON; 'Rundown' rearranges ILTON with ROBES.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunter constellation's waist is marked by three bright stars in a row, the famous asterism.

clue.text: Statue possibly of Greek character included in import

indicators.note: included in means the letter goes inside the word for import

parts.note: moment means importance, as in a matter of great moment
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure carved in stone, perhaps, and imported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'import' means significance (MOMENT), not shipping goods in.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is one example of a memorial structure, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Peacekeeping organisation's soldier invested in diamonds, perhaps — not helpful

parts.note: UNO is the United Nations Organisation, which sends peacekeepers

indicators.note: invested in means the soldier is placed inside the jewellery word

parts.note: bling is flashy jewellery, of which diamonds are an example
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A UN peacekeeper puts money into gems and is no help to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' suggests money but here means placed inside. Bling is slang for showy jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will not do favours or help out is described as disobliging or uncooperative.

clue.text: Digital coverage to be reinforced?

parts.note: digital means relating to digits, toes; the steel cap over the toes of a work boot strengthens it

explanation.surface: Sounds like a call to strengthen broadband or online news coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' looks electronic but refers to toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot's protective front piece, often steel, covers the toes, so it is coverage for digits that is reinforced.

clue.text: Local authority depositing gold in branch

indicators.note: depositing tells us the gold is placed somewhere
in places the gold inside the word for branch

parts.note: a bough is a large branch of a tree
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A council stashes its gold in a branch office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branch' suggests a bank office but is a tree's limb; gold is the heraldic word.
explanation.definitionFit: A town or district with its own council is a unit of local government.

clue.text: Employee of 17 working nights brings in union and head of management

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new arrangement
head of means the first letter of management

explanation.surface: A night-shift worker at the club signs up with the union and the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings in' joins U and M (head of 'management') into the letters of NIGHTS, all rearranged ('working'). 17 is ARSENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal makes or stores weapons, so a craftsman who makes firearms would work there.

clue.text: Bottom line's about North American military-industrial complex

indicators.note: about means going around the abbreviation for North American

parts.note: arse is British slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: The bottom line on America's military-industrial complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the bottom and the line letter around the North American abbreviation. ARSE is British slang for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a place, often a large site, where weapons and munitions are made or stored.

clue.text: Covered passage from Catholic hymnal initially, having gone outside

indicators.note: outside means the departure word goes round the other letters

parts.note: away means gone, as in out of the house
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of hymnal

explanation.surface: A churchgoer slips out of the vaulted passage with a hymnbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gone outside' reads as a departure but places the word for gone around the Catholic letters and the hymnal initial.
explanation.definitionFit: An archway is a passage beneath an arch, covered overhead by the curved structure.

clue.text: Cuckoo to exclude monarch

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A cuckoo pushes the reigning bird out of the nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' is not the bird but slang for mad; 'barking' (short for barking mad) is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal ways of calling someone crazy, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Hot cake left out once

indicators.note: out once means one of the two copies of the letter is dropped

parts.note: stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas

explanation.surface: A warm cake was once abandoned on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: STOLLEN has two Ls; only one goes, as 'once' says. 'Hot' is slang for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are hot have been recently stolen and are risky to sell, a criminal slang sense.

clue.text: Old prog rockers met up for church

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: ELP, Emerson, Lake and Palmer, the 1970s progressive rock band

explanation.surface: Ageing prog rock musicians got together for a church reunion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ELP + MET backwards, giving TEM + PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a place of worship; in French Protestant usage a church is called one.

clue.text: Last of veteran Apple Macs is recycled — they've no memory left

indicators.note: recycled suggests the letters being broken down and reused in a new form
last of takes the final letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Old Apple computers go for recycling once their memory is used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of' gives N and E; 'recycled' rearranges these with MACS IS.
explanation.definitionFit: People with amnesia have lost their memory, so they have none left, a plural noun.

clue.text: Neither piece is one of those who famously skewered king

definitions.text: one of those who famously skewered king

parts.note: nor pairs with neither, as in neither this nor that
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Neither chess piece is the one that took down the king.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1066 the Norman invaders killed King Harold, by tradition with an arrow in the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans defeated Harold II at Hastings, the king traditionally pierced by an arrow.

clue.text: Spin doctor puts 'Morph's a beauty' before 'dissolute rake'

parts.note: Morph is the setter, so Morph's means I am, shortened to I'm
a gem is a beauty, something precious

indicators.note: dissolute means loose, so the letters of rake are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: A PR man announces the setter is lovely and a dissolute rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morph's' becomes I'M, since the setter refers to themself.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor manages a politician's public reputation, crafting how they look to voters.

clue.text: Women ensnared by wicked madam

indicators.note: ensnared by means caught inside the word for wicked

parts.note: bad means wicked

explanation.surface: Young women are trapped by a cruel brothel keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A bawd is an old word for a woman who runs a brothel, which is what madam means here.

clue.text: Count to exclude monarch

parts.note: to ban someone is to exclude them
K is an abbreviation for king, a monarch

explanation.surface: A nobleman sets out to depose the sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' is not a nobleman but a verb: to count on is to bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to rely or count on it.

clue.text: Exercise, gaining weight on diet of fish?

parts.note: the plank is a core-strengthening exercise held face down
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone working out but putting on weight wonders whether to eat fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' joins the two pieces. The question mark flags that whales and many fish feed on these drifting organisms.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny drifting organisms in the sea are the food of many fish and whales, hence their diet.

clue.text: Badgers picked up a sound

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a microphone picks up a sound

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; a sound is a noise

explanation.surface: The badgers picked up a sound in the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badgers' is a verb, not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them, which irritates them; a verb in the third person.
